first_answer:
The error shown on the screen is "error[E0499]: cannot borrow `x` as mutable more than once." This error occurs when trying to borrow a mutable variable (`x`) more than once, which is not allowed in Rust.

To rebuild the project, you would click on the "Rebuild" button.

VISUAL_TOKEN_BUDGET_FINDING.what_the_old_eval_missed: this file measured ONE fixture with unusually large text and judged quality by eyeballing a single answer string. That never surfaced the defect below.
VISUAL_TOKEN_BUDGET_FINDING.the_defect: a 1512x982 screen is ~1890 Qwen2-VL visual tokens, and feeding that many drives this checkpoint into REPETITION COLLAPSE on ordinary screenshots. Asked for the IPv4 address on a legible settings dialog it answered 'The The The The The ...'; asked what a button said on a code-editor screenshot it did the same; asked for an error code it regurgitated the source.
VISUAL_TOKEN_BUDGET_FINDING.the_fix: cap the image at DESCRIBE_IMAGE_MAX_PIXELS = 380000 (~764x496, ~459 visual tokens) before generating. Aspect-ratio preserving; images already under the cap are untouched; any failure returns the original path so it costs the speedup and never the answer.

before_after_single_samples.orig_error_code_before: 7945 ms, describes the borrow error but gives no code

the_working_band.floor: ~216 visual tokens (0.35 scale) - accuracy 0/8, text unreadable

VISUAL_TOKEN_BUDGET_FINDING.WHAT_THIS_DOES_NOT_FIX: screen-VQA is still not reliable. Across three fixtures and four checkable facts the model scored 2/12 to 4/12 at EVERY resolution, and even after the cap it hallucinated an error code that is not on screen. The cap removes a failure MODE and 5x of latency; it does not make this 2B checkpoint good at reading screens. A better VLM is the real answer and remains unevaluated.
